title: Healing and Improving Postnatal Nights Through Sleep (HIPNoS)
official: Healing and Improving Postnatal Nights Through Sleep (HIPNoS): A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Perinatal Understanding of Mindful Awareness for Sleep (PUMAS) in Postpartum Women With Insomnia and Depression.
summary: Insomnia and depression are highly prevalent during postpartum, but effective treatment options are severely limited. Perinatal Understanding of Mindful Awareness (PUMAS) combines behavioral sleep strategies and mindfulness-based exercises to improve sleep and mood during pregnancy. Indeed, PUMAS has been shown to effectively treatment comorbid insomnia and depression in pregnancy in controlled and uncontrolled trials. The present randomized controlled trial (RCT) will evaluate the effectiveness of PUMAS in a sample of postpartum women with comorbid insomnia and depression who will be randomized to to telemedicine PUMAS or online sleep hygiene education (SHE; enhanced usual care). Patients will be treated for six weeks followed by assessment after treatment then follow-up assessment 3-months later. The investigators hypothesize that PUMAS patients, relative to SHE patients, will report superior acute treatment effects on insomnia and depression as well as more durable effects at 3-month follow-up.

interventions.name: Perinatal Understanding of Mindful Awareness for Sleep (PUMAS)

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participant is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the trial
* Participant must be able to engage in treatment (e.g., has internet access to attend telemedicine appointments or access online sleep hygiene materials).
* Aged 18 years or above.
* Postpartum 4-12 months at time of screening.
* Meets diagnostic criteria for DSM-5 insomnia disorder, acute (symptoms lasting ≥1 month).
* Clinically severe insomnia symptom severity (Insomnia Severity Index score ≥11).
* Clinically significant depression symptoms (Edinburg Postnatal Depression Scale score ≥10).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Sleep complaints primarily due to infant sleep problems as ascertained via clinical interview and/or describing the infant's sleep as a 'moderate' or 'serious' problem on the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire on the screening survey.
* Suicidal intent per the Columbus Suicide Severity Rating Scale (Suicidal ideation WITHOUT intent is NOT exclusionary).
* Current engagement in psychotherapy for insomnia disorder (current use of sleep aids \[prescription, over-the-counter, or dietary supplements\] is NOT exclusionary).
* Night or rotating shift work.
* Unreliable internet access that prevents a patient from being to engage with treatment and/or assessments.
